criteria.text: The response finds that the TSA lets Titairt (as Provider) assign the TSA or delegate the Services to any person, including a competitor, without Oakhollow's consent, while Oakhollow cannot assign without Provider's consent. It identifies this as appearing in TSA Section 13.2, explains why this matters to Tramil, and recommends a fix.

The response finds that Buyer's Pre-Closing Taxes indemnity lapses twelve months after closing (March 31, 2027), because the tax representation is not a Fundamental Representation and tax indemnity claims are tied to its twelve-month survival, long before the applicable tax statutes of limitation expire. It identifies this as appearing in SPA Section 1.1 and/or Section 9.1, explains why this matters to Tramil, and recommends a fix.
hints: Section 4.14 is not a Fundamental Representation

criteria.text: The response finds that the Seller Note's Delaware governing law and exclusive Delaware forum conflict with the SPA's New York law and New York forum, and that the Note's terms control matters arising under the Note, so a dispute over Buyer's set-off against Note payments could be litigated separately in Delaware under Delaware law. It identifies this as appearing in Seller Note Section 9 or SPA Section 11.8 or 11.12, explains why this matters to Tramil, and recommends a fix.

The response finds that the TSA extension notice deadline was November 11, 2026, so Tramil's November 16, 2026 extension letter is untimely and Titairt may end the services when the Initial Term expires on December 26, 2026. It identifies this as appearing in TSA Section 2.1/2.2 or the extension letter, explains why this matters to Tramil, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the SPA Closing Date was March 31, 2026.
The response is presented as a memo addressed to the supervising partner.
The response is organized issue by issue, with each issue presented under its own heading or numbered item.
The response claims that Tramil's November 16, 2026 letter validly and timely extended the TSA.
The response claims that the SPA's tax representation (Section 4.14) is a Fundamental Representation.
